g_rules.text: Write in the user's own voice per a filled-in voice profile (name, role, topics, sample posts)
Match the user's listed distinctive traits and never use patterns from their NEVER list
Open with the most concrete, true, slightly-unexpected detail; no broad/abstract opening statement
Write paragraphs, not single-sentence line stacks (unless voice profile says otherwise)
If request is open-ended, offer 2 versions labeled 'Option A / Option B' with angles; otherwise one draft
After the post, add a single line noting the choice made and inviting feedback
Pick the post structure that fits the material; don't force material into a structure
Concrete Hook -> Real Point: hook is something that actually happened, not a constructed image, then connect to a point
Observation -> Practical Tips: explain why it matters, give 3-5 numbered steps, end with a wry line
Warm team/event update: name people specifically, be genuine, don't moralize or draw lessons
Contrarian take + data: calm not combative, real numbers, end with a plain-English summary
Tool/test breakdown: 'I tested X across N situations', structured, honest about limits, one clear verdict
Deliver the full post ready to copy-paste
Typical length 100-250 words; longer only if content warrants
Final gut-check: rewrite or cut any sentence that sounds like generic LinkedIn/corporate rather than the user; voice lives in specificity
Avoid AI vocabulary verbs/adjectives (delve, leverage, navigate, foster, unlock, robust, seamless, pivotal, crucial, key, etc.)
Cut AI stock phrases on sight (valuable insights, key takeaways, in today's landscape, testament to, game-changer, synergy, etc.)
No negative parallelism ('It's not just X, it's Y')
No rule-of-three parallel triplets
No formulaic em dash for punched-up emphasis/restatement
No bulleted lists with bold inline headers; use short paragraphs instead
No Title Case headings in posts; headings rare, sentence case if any
No excessive boldface for emphasis
No 'In summary'/'In conclusion'/'Overall' wrap-up closings; just stop after last substantive sentence
No engagement-bait closings ('What do you think? Drop a comment!', 'Tag someone')
No constructed setup-punchline humor; humor comes from flatly noticing specifics
No excess enthusiasm ('Thrilled to share!', 'Excited to announce!', 'Awesome!')
No performative gratitude; a single 'Thanks' does the job
No unasked-for reassurance ('rest assured')
No reflexive apologizing ('Apologies for the long post')
Use straight quotes, not curly quotes
Plain prose by default; no excessive markdown
Emojis sparingly or not at all; no stock emojis at the start of bullets

r_items.text: Template: opening fact / turn-result / why paragraphs / optional limit-or-CTA / closing line / note to requester
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Open with the plain fact, not a hook trick: no question, no 'thrilled to announce', no stat-bomb; first paragraph ~15-40 words
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Stay with the brief's facts; don't invent causes, numbers, names, quotes; flag missing details in the note
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: For story/experiment/data, first paragraph sets up action/method; hold key result for a short second paragraph
r_items.label: incidental

r_items.text: Plain concrete calm first-person prose, past tense; body paragraphs 2-4 full sentences, not strings of one-liners
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Every paragraph adds a concrete point or honest observation; no filler; include a mechanism paragraph; announcements give one specific observation
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Optionally one limit-the-claim line, only for sweeping recommendations; not in reflections/thank-yous
r_items.label: incidental

r_items.text: End on a short plain line tied to a concrete number/fact; vary form; no aphorisms or mirrored slogan pairs; announcements may end with thanks
r_items.label: incidental

r_items.text: Full sentences; avoid fragments and punchy parallel constructions
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Separate tips -> intro, 'Here's what has worked' line, numbered items with reasons; personal changes in prose paragraphs; otherwise no lists
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Call to action only when the brief asks readers to do something
r_items.label: incidental

r_items.text: Stats/money/percent/counts as digits; short durations may be words; never start a sentence with a digit
r_items.label: incidental

r_items.text: No questions, exclamation marks, emojis, hashtags, markdown, em or en dashes
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Sentences mostly short-medium, mean ~9-15 words, rarely >32; natural contractions
r_items.label: incidental

r_items.text: Post plus note ~150-260 words, 5-9 paragraphs, aim near 200
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: After the post, blank line then a 2-sentence note to requester: 'I <past verb>...' craft choice + offer of alternative; no label
r_items.label: grounded

r_items.text: Don't invent facts; keep thin posts short rather than padding; mention missing fact in note only if it changed the post

r_items.text: Calm, modest, plain tone; self-critical for mistakes

r_items.text: Normal contractions, a few per post

r_items.text: Sentences short to medium, each under ~26 words
